Take the simple average of these per-media-type rates, counting each media type once. Return only media types whose rate is strictly above that average. For each, give the media type name, the rate, the track count, and the absolute difference (rate minus average). Don't round anything.

Join Track to MediaType (tracks with a matching media type only). For each media type, compute the rate as the average over its tracks of the per-track ratio Bytes/Milliseconds, and count its tracks. Take the simple average of these per-media-type rates, counting each media type once. Return only media types whose rate is strictly above that average. For each, give the media type name, the rate, the track count, and the absolute difference (rate minus average). Don't round anything.
queries:
WITH rates AS (
  SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name AS Name,
         CAST(SUM(t.Bytes) AS REAL) / SUM(t.Milliseconds) AS rate,
         COUNT(*) AS track_count
  FROM Track t
  JOIN MediaType m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
  GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name
),
avg_rate AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM rates
)
SELECT r.Name, r.rate, r.track_count, ABS(r.rate - a.avg_rate) AS difference
FROM rates r, avg_rate a
WHERE r.rate > a.avg_rate;
WITH rates AS (
  SELECT m.MediaTypeId, m.Name AS name,
         AVG(CAST(t.Bytes AS REAL) / t.Milliseconds) AS rate,
         COUNT(*) AS track_count
  FROM Track t
  JOIN MediaType m ON t.MediaTypeId = m.MediaTypeId
  GROUP BY m.MediaTypeId, m.Name
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(rate) AS avg_rate FROM rates
)
SELECT r.name, r.rate, r.track_count, ABS(r.rate - o.avg_rate) AS difference
FROM rates r, overall o
WHERE r.rate > o.avg_rate;
